title: Normalized proper-open interchange respects successive proper maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves and finite-subextension convention [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ for the ordinary unbounded categories and use the module operations of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories; sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback; sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Let $p:P\to Y$ and $h:P'\to P$ be proper, let $i:Y\hookrightarrow B$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$$P\xrightarrow{u}W\xrightarrow{r}B,\qquad P'\xrightarrow{v}W'\xrightarrow{s}W$$
be dense compactifications of $ip$ and $uh$, respectively, meaning $u,v$ are quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dense open immersions, $r,s$ proper, $ru=ip$ and $sv=uh$ [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. For every $A\in D_{P'}$, let
$$I_{Rh_*A}:i_!Rp_*Rh_*A\to Rr_*u_!Rh_*A,\quad J_A:u_!Rh_*A\to Rs_*v_!A,$$
$$I'_A:i_!R(ph)_*A\to R(rs)_*v_!A$$
be the normalized maps of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), for $(p,i,u,r)$, $(h,u,v,s)$ and $(ph,i,v,rs)$, respectively. Here normalized means that after open restriction and the canonical restriction identifications, composition with the open-extension unit is the identity of the proper direct image. Then the following equality holds for every unbounded $A$, naturally in $A$:
$$\kappa_{r,s,v_!A}\circ I'_A\circ i_!(\kappa_{p,h,A}^{-1})=Rr_*(J_A)\circ I_{Rh_*A}:i_!Rp_*Rh_*A\to Rr_*Rs_*v_!A,$$
where $\kappa$ denotes the canonical derived direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. No finite-Tor, constructibility or localizing-closure hypothesis on $A$ is required for this equality of maps.
